does: Cooks food under hot oil, so that its surface dries to a crisp shell while the inside steams.

intro.what: Food cooks submerged in hot oil while its surface dries into a crisp shell.
intro.why: Oil heat and crowding affect the crust. Managing batches helps the surface crisp instead of becoming heavy and greasy.

how: Dry the food well. Water makes hot oil spit and boil over.
Fill a deep, heavy pan no more than a third full of oil and heat it.
Lower in a small batch, so that the oil keeps its heat and the pieces do not stick together.
Lift the food out when it is crisp and golden, drain it on a rack and salt it at once.
For thick chips, fry once gently until soft and pale, rest them, then fry again in hotter oil until crisp.

cues.text: A steady stream of small bubbles around each piece, slowing as the food dries and turns golden.
A lively, even crackle. A loud spit means water, and silence means the oil is too cool.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the oil cools and the food soaks it up and turns greasy.
mistakes.fix: Fry in small batches and let the oil come back to heat between them.

mistakes.mistake: Putting wet food into the oil, so that it spits and foams up.
mistakes.fix: Pat everything dry first, and never fill the pan more than a third.

mistakes.mistake: Oil that smokes. It tastes acrid and is close to catching fire.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat at once and let it cool.

quiz.question: What produces the crisp shell during deep-frying?
choices: The surface absorbs water until it swells.
The food surface loses moisture in the hot oil.
The surface stays wet beneath a cool oil film.
quiz.because: The drying surface becomes the crust while moisture within the food produces steam.

quiz.question: How should a crowded load of food be handled?
choices: Add it all together to cool the oil quickly.
Keep adding food as the bubbling slows.
Divide it into smaller batches and let the oil recover between them.
quiz.because: Smaller batches limit the drop in oil heat and reduce pieces sticking together.

quiz.question: Which sound fits the intended frying action?
choices: A lively even crackle around the food.
Complete silence around a newly added batch.
Violent spitting from a wet surface.
quiz.because: An even crackle reflects the active frying described here; silence and harsh spitting suggest different conditions.

quiz.question: The crust was greasy after the pan was crowded. What would you change for the next batch?
choices: Crowd the pan more tightly next time.
Fry smaller batches with recovery between them.
Keep lowering the heat while adding more food.
quiz.because: Crowding cools the oil and undermines the drying and crisping of the surface.

variant_of.differs: The food is covered by the oil and floats in it. Nothing touches the pan.
